question: Should Slack preserve the documented separate-progress delivery mode while using the shared typed progress pipeline, or should tool-progress suppression intentionally become universal?
rationale: The patch crosses the Codex producer, generic reply payload, and Slack renderer while changing observable delivery for an existing preference; repository evidence does not safely establish that universal suppression is the intended permanent contract.

options.title: Preserve separate progress
options.body: Use the shared typed progress pipeline and suppress or react only when the effective Slack streaming configuration requests that behavior.

options.title: Make suppression universal
options.body: Intentionally redefine the existing preference, update its documentation and compatibility expectations, and provide upgrade-focused proof.

options.title: Narrow the PR
options.body: Remove the new cross-plugin discriminator and retain only delivery-state fixes until the shared progress contract is settled separately.

recommendation.title: Preserve separate progress
recommendation.body: Use the shared typed progress pipeline and suppress or react only when the effective Slack streaming configuration requests that behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most strongly connects this contributor to Slack and shared streaming progress semantics.
